name: Budgeting v2 — Automation & UX Improvements
description: A local Flask/SQLite app for personal finance tracking. Ingests bank/credit card statements (CSV or PDF), categorizes transactions via merchant rules and a local Ollama LLM, and provides a web UI for review and analysis. This PRD covers automation of the monthly import workflow, smarter rule matching with detail-aware patterns, and a batch review UI to eliminate the one-at-a-time edit loop.
qualityGates: flake8 app/ passes with no errors
flask run starts without errors against a migrated SQLite database
No secrets, personal data, or database files committed to the repository

userStories.title: pytest test suite baseline
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a pytest test suite covering the core categorization logic, rule matching, and CSV import so that regressions are caught automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: Branch eumaeus/budgeting-improvements checked out from main before any changes
tests/ directory exists with conftest.py and at least one test file
Tests use an in-memory SQLite database (no real DB required)

Coverage includes: apply_rules with no detail_pattern, apply_rules with matching detail_pattern, apply_rules with non-matching detail_pattern, import-csv with duplicate fingerprint skipping, normalize_description and extract_merchant for known patterns
pytest passes with no failures
flake8 app/ passes
userStories.notes: There is currently no test suite at all. This must be the first thing implemented — all subsequent stories depend on pytest passing. Branch must be created before any code changes.

userStories.title: Detail-aware merchant rules
userStories.description: As a user, I want merchant rules to optionally match on transaction detail text (not just merchant name) so that a single merchant like Sam's Club can map to different categories depending on what was purchased (gas vs groceries vs clothing).
acceptanceCriteria: MerchantRule model gains a nullable detail_pattern column (substring or regex, case-insensitive)
Alembic migration created and applies cleanly against existing database
Rule matching updated: merchant pattern matched first, then detail_pattern applied if present
More specific rules (with detail_pattern) take priority over fallback rules (detail_pattern IS NULL) for the same merchant
If no rule matches, LLM categorization proceeds as before
flask categorize --create-rules still works and creates rules without detail_pattern (broad fallback rules)
flake8 app/ passes
pytest passes with tests covering: rule with no detail_pattern, rule with matching detail_pattern, rule with non-matching detail_pattern falling through to LLM
userStories.notes: detail_pattern matching should use Python re.search (case-insensitive) against transaction.description_clean. Merchant match continues to use substring as before. Sam's Club example: detail_pattern='UNLEADED|GALLONS|GAS' -> Gas, detail_pattern=NULL -> Groceries (fallback).

userStories.title: Batch inline category review on import detail page
userStories.description: As a user reviewing an import, I want to change transaction categories inline without a full page reload per transaction so that I can categorize an entire import in one pass instead of submitting one form at a time.
acceptanceCriteria: Import detail page category dropdowns save via fetch/XHR on change — no submit button required
Row updates visually (category name, source badge) after successful save without full page reload
Error state shown inline if save fails
Existing POST /imports/:id/transactions/:tx_id/set-category endpoint updated to return JSON (already partially done — ensure it returns ok, tx_id, category_id, category_name, category_source)
Create rule checkbox still present and functional (submitted alongside category change)
flake8 app/ passes
pytest passes
userStories.notes: The set-category route already returns JSON. The frontend change is the main work: wire the select onChange to fetch, update the row DOM on success. Keep the form markup for graceful degradation if JS fails.

userStories.title: Filter import review to uncategorized / model-categorized transactions
userStories.description: As a user reviewing an import, I want to filter the transaction list to show only uncategorized or LLM-categorized transactions so that I can focus my review on uncertain items and skip the ones already handled by rules.
acceptanceCriteria: Import detail page has filter toggle: All / Needs Review (uncategorized + model-sourced) / Uncategorized only
Filter applies client-side (JS hide/show) — no page reload required
Transaction count shown per filter state (e.g. '12 of 47 shown')
Filter state persisted in URL hash or query param so it survives page refresh
flake8 app/ passes
pytest passes
userStories.notes: Rows already have category_source available in the template. Add data-source attribute to each row and filter via JS. This dramatically reduces review time for large imports where most transactions are rule-matched.

userStories.title: Rule promotion after import confirmation
userStories.description: As a user, after confirming an import I want to be prompted to promote recurring LLM-categorized merchants to rules so that future imports for those merchants are handled automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: After POST /imports/:id/confirm, redirect to a rule promotion page instead of back to import detail
Promotion page lists unique merchants from the import where category_source='model', grouped by merchant + assigned category
Each row has a checkbox (default checked) and an optional detail_pattern input field
Submitting the form creates MerchantRule entries for checked rows
Merchants that already have a matching rule are excluded from the list
If no promotable merchants exist, skip the promotion page and redirect to /imports
flake8 app/ passes
pytest passes
userStories.notes: This is the key habit-building loop: each confirmed import makes future imports faster. The detail_pattern input lets Brett add specificity (e.g. for Sam's Club transactions) at promotion time.

userStories.title: process-statement orchestration command
userStories.description: As a user, I want a single flask process-statement command that accepts a file (PDF or CSV) and account ID and automatically runs pdf-to-csv (if needed), import-csv, and categorize in sequence so that I can process a monthly statement in one step.
acceptanceCriteria: flask process-statement --account-id <id> --file <path> command exists
Auto-detects PDF vs CSV by file extension
For PDFs: runs pdf-to-csv with auto format detection, writes to a temp file, then imports the temp CSV
For CSVs: imports directly
Runs flask categorize after import (default limit=500, create-rules=false)
Prints a summary: transactions imported, skipped, categorized by rule, categorized by model, uncategorized
Exits non-zero if any step fails
flake8 app/ passes
pytest passes
userStories.notes: This eliminates steps 2-4 of the current monthly workflow. PDF temp file should be written to a system temp dir and cleaned up after import. The command should be composable — individual sub-commands (pdf-to-csv, import-csv, categorize) remain usable standalone.

userStories.title: Rule management UI
userStories.description: As a user, I want a UI page to view, edit, and delete merchant rules so that I can fix bad rules without touching the database directly.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /rules lists all MerchantRules with pattern, detail_pattern, and category
Each rule has an edit link and a delete button
Edit form allows updating pattern, detail_pattern, and category
Delete removes the rule with a confirmation step
flake8 app/ passes
pytest passes
userStories.notes: Currently rules can only be created via CLI or the import detail page. There's no way to fix or remove a bad rule without a flask shell. This is a frequent pain point.
